Statute Lookup

Ohio Revised Code sections on the current Hamilton County roster
Arrest is not conviction. Everyone listed here is legally presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty in a court of law. Charges are accusations only. Tiers shown are the statutory default for the cited section. The degree actually charged in a case can be heavier or lighter based on subsections, prior offenses, and aggravating factors determined by the charging authority or the court.

Tap a section to see who is currently held under it, its plain-English meaning, the statutory max term, and where it sits on Ohio's severity ladder. 198 sections appear on the current roster of 1,159 people in custody. Statutes are linked to codes.ohio.gov, the official source maintained by the Ohio Legislative Service Commission. Felony cases are heard in the Court of Common Pleas, General Division; misdemeanors in Hamilton County Municipal Court. People charged with a crime who cannot afford an attorney are entitled to one through the Hamilton County Public Defender (513-946-3700).

F5 § 2925.11 Possession of drugs 220 held · 19.0%

Possession of drugs. Knowingly obtaining, possessing, or using a controlled substance or controlled substance analog. The most common felony charge in Hamilton County.

Severity: F5 default for most schedules. Ladders by substance/weight up to F1.

M1 § 2913.02 Theft 166 held · 14.3%

Theft. Knowingly obtaining or exerting control over another's property without consent, by deception, threat, or intimidation, with purpose to deprive. The tier escalates with the dollar value: under $1,000 is M1; $1,000-$7,500 is F5; up to F1 for $1.5M+.

Severity: M1 default — up to 180 days. Felony at $1,000+.

M1 § 2903.13 Assault 153 held · 13.2%

Assault. Knowingly causing or attempting to cause physical harm to another, OR recklessly causing serious physical harm. Bar fights, simple punches.

Severity: M1 — up to 180 days jail, $1,000 fine. Becomes a felony against certain victims (officers, EMS, teachers).

M2 § 2921.31 Obstructing official business 138 held · 11.9%

Obstructing official business. Without privilege, doing any act that hampers or impedes a public official in performance of lawful duties. Refusing to identify, fleeing a stop, blocking arrest of another.

Severity: M2 default — up to 90 days. F5 if it creates risk of physical harm.
